—I have no choice. I must find out what Fuji is up to in there.

For the sake of a peaceful dinner tonight—and, by extension, for Saber, who is secretly looking forward to it!

“Pardon me… Oh, you’re making okonomiyaki. Hungry for a snack, Fuji?”

“No. Sakura left dinner to me, so I’m on duty tonight. I’m making enough for all three of us. You go wake Saber.”

“Excuse me… Oh, okonomiyaki? Are you hungry?”
“You’re wrong. Sakura-chan left me in charge, so I’ll be cooking tonight. I’ll cook for all three of us, so can you go wake Saber-chan up?”

“Of course we will. We’re having crab omelet tonight. Without rice, it would just be an ordinary omelet.”

So saying, she cracks an egg.

It drops into the bowl, where the flour she dissolved earlier eddies in a thick, gluey mass.

pages.en:
“—Fuji. You’ll realize your mistake on your own in a few minutes, but I’m going to summon my courage and tell you now.”

“Ugh… W-what? Fine. I’ll listen, so please, enlighten me.”

She must have suspected that something was wrong herself. Despite her bluster, Fuji turns to me with admirable humility.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Fuji-nee. I know you’ll realize your mistake in a few minutes, but I’ll come out and tell you.”
“Uh… W-What? All right, tell me.”
She must think something’s wrong as well.
She looks at me with respect.

pages.en:
“All right. That is not crab omelet. All you are creating is the most horrifying okonomiyaki rice bowl the world has ever seen. Let’s start over.”

I deliver the verdict without hesitation.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well. That’s not kani-tama. It’ll be a horrifying dish where you’ll be putting okonomiyaki on top of rice. So let’s remake this.”
I clearly tell her.

「違う。そもそも俺はコック長ではない。このままだとセイバーに間違った日本料理を学習させる事になるんで、やり直そう」
はい、と藤ねえからボールを取り上げる。

pages.en:
“Hmph… Is putting okonomiyaki on rice really so different from putting an omelet on it, Chef Shirou?”

“Yes. And I am not your head chef. At this rate, Saber is going to learn completely fictitious Japanese cuisine. We’re starting over.”

“Hand it over.”

I take the bowl from Fuji.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hmm… Isn’t it the same putting omelet or okonomiyaki on rice, kitchen chief?”
“No. First of all, I’m not a kitchen chief. We’ll give Saber a wrong impression of Japanese food, so let’s remake this.”
I take the bowl away from Fuji-nee.

“Ehehe. You have such authority when you’re in the kitchen, Shirou.”

With that, she opens the refrigerator.

“Hm…”

I admit I enjoy being told I have authority. But should I really be pleased when it only applies in the kitchen?
